mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen from -13.0 to -5.3 over the last two weeks, indicating an underlying recovery trend in discretionary mobility that should continue mechanically for the next four weeks absent a new shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -13.0 at t-1w to -5.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the last 28-day mean despite the two-week rising streak observed at the decision point.

mechanism_narrative: Transit stations mobility remaining suppressed below -30 percent for multiple weeks signals ongoing restriction or avoidance of public transport, which constrains access to retail precincts and depresses RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -30 for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -36.3 at t-3w and -34.4 at t-1w, both below -30
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days even though TRANSIT remains below -30 for two or more consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES mobility drops sharply while RESIDENTIAL mobility rises in the same week, this joint pattern reflects a stay-at-home behavioral shift that reduces incidental retail trips, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to weeks where the two series move independently.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 20 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL rises in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -6.6 to -36.7 at t-1w while RESIDENTIAL rose from 2.0 to 7.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the following 28 days despite a joint WORKPLACES drop and RESIDENTIAL rise meeting the trigger threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A substitution effect occurs when PARKS mobility rises while TRANSIT mobility falls in the same period, indicating households are shifting discretionary outings to nearby outdoor spaces instead of transit-dependent retail districts, which suppresses RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 15 points week-on-week while TRANSIT simultaneously falls
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -12.4 to 9.9 at t-1w while TRANSIT fell from -25.4 to -34.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days despite PARKS rising sharply and TRANSIT falling in the same week.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has stayed persistently positive across all four weeks, reflecting a seasonal pattern of extended at-home time that structurally caps retail and recreation recovery over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remained positive in all four weeks (6.6, 2.0, 7.0, 3.9)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL remains positive throughout the same window.

mechanism_narrative: Sharp week-to-week swings in GROCERY_PHARM mobility reflect stockpiling or restocking cycles that temporarily substitute for discretionary retail trips, producing a short one-week dip in RETAIL_REC immediately following a GROCERY_PHARM spike.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM changes by more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM swung from -1.7 to 7.7 and then to -9.4 across consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week following a GROCERY_PHARM swing exceeding 10 points, across repeated observations.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-week collapse in WORKPLACES mobility followed by partial recovery the next week indicates a short-lived restriction episode (e.g., a public holiday or brief lockdown order); as WORKPLACES mobility recovers, RETAIL_REC should rebound within one week due to restored commuting-linked shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES drops more than 20 points week-on-week then partially recovers the following week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell to -36.7 at t-1w then recovered to -15.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the week following a WORKPLACES partial recovery after a prior sharp drop.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has oscillated between deep negative and positive values across the snapshot, indicating a mean-reverting activity pattern; this oscillation historically co-moves with RETAIL_REC recovery phases, implying RETAIL_REC will continue its reversion toward less negative values over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -42.7 to -12.4 to 9.9 to -5.6 over the four weeks, showing mean reversion
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 28-day mean fails to rise even as PARKS continues its mean-reverting oscillation pattern.
